paper_title: A Complexity-Theoretic Approach to Proofs of Space
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 5
statement: Because the SNARG forces comparison to the verifier chosen y = f (x), the Merkle tree only requires 2nd pre-image resistance and hence can be instantiated from one-way functions [AR23]. (However, we do not know appropriate succinct arguments from such assumptions.) Additionally, the succinct argument requires a particular structure which is not shared by all doubly efficient proof systems: the prover can effectively preprocess the whole proving strategy into a succinct state, which can be quickly used when interacting with the verifier. While we do not know how to adapt certain recursive proof systems to this framework, such as [RRR16], this is a feature of Kilian’s classic PCP-based argument and any SNARG (as well as [GKR08], but this imposes undesirable structural limitations).
context: We note that this naive recipe is only possible because f is an explicit function (and does not rely on the random oracle)! Because the SNARG forces comparison to the verifier chosen y = f (x), the Merkle tree only requires 2nd pre-image resistance and hence can be instantiated from one-way functions [AR23]. (However, we do not know appropriate succinct arguments from such assumptions.) Additionally, the succinct argument requires a particular structure which is not shared by all doubly efficient proof systems: the prover can effectively preprocess the whole proving strategy into a succinct state, which can be quickly used when interacting with the verifier. While we do not know how to adapt certain recursive proof systems to this framework, such as [RRR16], this is a feature of Kilian’s classic PCP-based argument and any SNARG (as well as [GKR08], but this imposes undesirable structural limitations). Warm-up: constant soundness. To prove the soundness of this framework, we wish to show that if there exists a cheating prover strategy that maintains a small state and yet can convince the verifier to accept with non-negligible probability, then f must not have had high computational depth. In other words, given a cheating prover A that, on challenge x, produces a small state σx that convinces the verifier to accept, we want to show how to extract f (x) from the short description σx . However, the key challenge, for this to be a contradiction, our extractor must run in time t.
